#1432. The neural basis of flavour–nutrient learning

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Animals learn about the external world in part through interoceptive signals1,2. For example, the nutrient content of food is first estimated in the mouth, in the form of flavour, and then it is measured again through slower signals from the gut. How these signals from the mouth and gut are integrated to drive learning is unclear. Here we identify a dopamine (DA) pathway that enables learning about the nutrient content of food. We show that DA neurons in the ventral tegmental area are necessary for associating nutrients with flavours, and that post-ingestive nutrients trigger DA release selectively in a small region of the anterior basolateral amygdala (BLA) but not in canonical DA targets in striatum. This nutrient-triggered DA release occurs preferentially in the left BLA in mice, and this same structure is preferentially activated by post-ingestive nutrients in humans. We identify the gut sensors that are responsible for nutrient-triggered DA release; show that they activate BLA-projecting DA neurons defined by expression of cholecystokinin; and demonstrate that stimulation of DA axon terminals in the anterior BLA drives flavour–nutrient learning but not other aspects of feeding behaviour. Two-photon imaging of neurons in the left anterior BLA reveals that they integrate gustatory and post-ingestive cues, and silencing these neurons prevents flavour–nutrient learning. These findings establish a neural basis for how animals learn about the nutrient content of their food.

Legends and additional references for Supplementary Tables 1–6.

Behaviour statistics. Summary information for all behavioural tests for each manipulation. Values are reported to 1 decimal place. Number of animals is reported as n. P values are reported for all statistical tests, and are shown in bold if below standard significance level (α = 0.05). In cases in which a Benjamini–Hochberg correction was made for multiple comparisons, an adjusted P value (p′) is shown (where p′ = P × m/i, where i is rank and m is number of cohorts tested; Methods). X′ corresponds to the normalized value of X. For self-stimulation, ‘presses’ means the number of inactive lever presses has been subtracted from the number of active lever presses. In flavour conditioning experiments in which mice began the test with >90% preference for one flavour, statistics are also provided (in parentheses) with these mice excluded. Permutation (perm.) tests use an exact test (or 100,000 iterations if n > 9) and are unpaired, unless otherwise mentioned (note: this means the lowest calculable P value is 1 × 10−5).

Dopamine imaging statistics. Summary information for all recordings of dopamine release in each brain region. Values are reported to 2 decimal places. Number of animals is reported as n. P values are reported for all statistical tests, and are shown in bold if below standard significance level (α = 0.05). X′ corresponds to the normalized value of X. For photometry traces, dF′/F′ means the dF/F values seen during sham infusion have been subtracted. For rise times, s′ means that the time is relative to approximate entry of liquid into the stomach. For fall times, s′ means that the time is relative to the end of the infusion. For peak times during licking, s′ means that the time is relative to the start of the first licking bout. The baseline is defined as the first 10 min of the recording for GI and post-GI measurements, or 0–20 s before the start of the first licking bout for oral measurements. Permutation tests use an exact test (or 100,000 iterations if n >9) and are unpaired, unless otherwise mentioned (note that this means the lowest calculable P value is 1 × 10−5).

Single-cell imaging statistics. Summary information for all 1- and 2-photon miniscope recordings. Values are reported to 2 decimal places. The number (n) of animals and number of cells are reported separately. P values are reported for all statistical tests, and are shown in bold if below standard significance level (α = 0.05). X′ corresponds to the normalized value of X. For rise times, s′ means that the time is relative to either the onset of the licking bout or to the approximate entry of liquid into the stomach. Population-weighted activity (pop-z) is calculated for a group of neurons (for example, activated or inhibited neurons) by multiplying activity by the fraction of neurons belonging to that group. Linear-mixed models (LME) treat mouse differences as both a fixed random effect and covariate (Methods). The relative contribution of mouse differences to total variance is reported by ICCs. Note that, for PCA, the number of PCs is equal to the number of cells. Permutation tests use an exact test (or 100,000 iterations if n > 9) and are unpaired, unless otherwise mentioned (note that this means that the lowest calculable P value for those tests is 1 × 10−5).

fMRI imaging statistics (n = 38). Activity from left and right BLA clusters binned every 2 min (20 min total), as shown in Extended Data Figs. 10f and 11n. For PET statistics, see ref. 56. Each of the ten time bins after glucose intake was contrasted against the baseline (2 min before glucose intake), representing the change in brain activity after glucose intake relative to the baseline. The contrast for the first effect was [ones(1,10)], and for the following contrasts [1], corresponding to the different time bins. The significance threshold was P < 0.05, FWE-corrected for multiple comparisons at the voxel level within the left or right BLA mask, respectively, with initial peak-level threshold set to P < 0.05 uncorrected.

Pseudorabies statistics. Regional labelling (load) was normalized to VTA load to control for injection efficiency. From the 1,328 annotated CCFv3 regions, only grey-matter areas were retained (372 total), with cortical layers collapsed into single structures. Regions smaller than 100 × 100 × 100 pixels were excluded to remove small nuclei with high variance from few labelled cells, yielding 131 analysed regions.

Brain connectivity tables. Connectivity matrices were generated manually, with each pair given a number indicating bidirectional projection strength from 0 (no known direct connection) to 5 (strongest projection known from this area). The connectivity strength between an area and itself was assigned a value of 5. For deciding what strength to assign a projection, large databases like the Allan Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas (ref. 1 of the Supplementary References) were preferred, supplemented by additional sources comprising reviews and anatomical tracing studies (refs. 2–32 of the Supplementary References).

#1430. Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

But then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent big players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

They hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

The question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

There was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the issue then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

“We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

The decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but big moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the plan of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

[On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

Changed the plan for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

We always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

It just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

He was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

Every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

Haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that shows personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”

“We had to change the plan a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”

And on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

There will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

But if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

What a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the big goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

Dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

Dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

Haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

United have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

Good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a big cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

Nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

City are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

It’s a big final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

We have now had an explanation and evidence of why the goal stood. The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

#MUNMCI – 59' VAR OVERTURNVAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball. pic.twitter.com/TyTip3ACIh

Enzo Fernandes’s shot from the edge of the D is tipped on to the post by Lammens! United are living dangerously, and Carrick has now thrown Sesko on in place of Tielemans.

Sesko on for United. Surprised he’s not come on before. City fans singing “Enzo, he’s in your head, Enzo, Enzo” to the tune of the Cranberries’ Zombie – and then he goes and hits a post.

What a final 30 minutes or so of football we have in store now. There will be an air of panic spreading through the United ranks, and Haaland, Ndiaye and Semenyo are still posing a threat.

Haaland and his City team-mates run off to celebrate in front of the away fans including Noel Gallagher.

The goalscorer looked marginally ahead of Dorgu and offside, but the camera angles can deceive. The reasoning for the final decision is not entirely clear.

United fans were goading and laughing at their City counterparts when the goal was initially ruled out for offside but it’s City who have had the last laugh.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

Sky are saying that VAR has concluded the striker is in an “onside position”.

It looks like they might be checking the position of Enzo Fernandez in the middle.

Haaland has the ball in the net but the flag is up for offside! Great finish at the back post from Gvardiol’s cross, but the City striker had just strayed offside. There is an ongoing VAR check, though.

City with a better sequence of passing but it does Ndiaye cannot get a shot away and then Fernandez commits another foul in midfield. Cunha with a poor cross behind for a City goal kick.

Bryan Mbeumo with a wild shot over the bar after cutting inside from the right, Mainoo was involved in propelling United forward once again. Then Cunha shoots over from a tight angle, but United are knocking on the door now.

Much better from United in the last few minutes, the crowd are engaged again and possibly for the first time in the game it feels like a goal might be coming. Nice idea from Rashford to let the ball run to Dorgu but the left-back is offside.

Kobbie Mainoo hits the post! Lovely strike from 25 yards after a Dalot pull-back is flicked into his path by Fernandes. Plenty of whip on it, and Donnarumma was beaten all ends up. Then United are back at the heart of the City defence, but Rashford’s shot deflects behind for a corner, from which the City goalkeeper is fouled.

He’s been United’s best player by a distance so far this season and Kobbie Mainoo goes very close there to giving United the lead with a fine strike that hits the post. Next passage of play and he releases Rashford in on the left whose shot is pushed out for a corner.

Kobbie Mainoo was INCHES from opening the scoring against Manchester United 🤏 pic.twitter.com/l9v8mlxzk3

Haaland does well to win City a free-kick in the United half after rolling Martinez. City had an early United corner to defend but they did so well. Quite a slow tempo to the game all round.

Fernandez’s deep delivery finds the unmarked Dias, and his header deflects behind for a City corner. Maguire heads away, and then Anderson’s cross drifts behind for a goal kick.

Strange moment as the game kicks-off while Sky’s Patrick Davison is still talking to Michael Carrick. He signs off in almost apologetic fashion for distracting the United manager from his job.

Ndiaye on for Cherki, so Maresca opting for a player who can dribble the ball over long distances.

Keane said: “For me, Fernandes is the player who has been violent. I don’t think that is a red card for Foden. Foden is a bit daft, but so is Bruno.”

Micah Richards said: “Because Foden doesn’t react in terms of, when he got kicked (by Fernandes) and started screaming on the floor, Fernandes would have been sent off. The fact Fernandes, as soon as he has touched him and there is minimal touching.. If Foden starts screaming the decision is reversed. As soon as Foden touches him Fernandes is screaming and rolling about the floor. Of course it (Foden kick) looks worse than it is. But I agree with Roy, Fernandes kicks him. As a player of course you are going to have some sort of reaction, I don’t agree with Foden’s reaction but Fernandes started it.”

This fixture has often brought out the best in Phil Foden but this is a third successive visit to Old Trafford he will want to forget. He was substituted at half-time of the 2-0 defeat in January with a broken hand and the season before he had been withdrawn before the hour mark after a poor performance in a 0-0 draw. And now sent off after 24 minutes.

A half that will be remembered for one thing and one thing only: Phil Foden’s red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

United were shading things before that flashpoint, but City will be pleased with their response to the sending off. They have defended well, and posed a threat going forward without executing the final pass or shot.

This is now a different game to the one United were expecting, so perhaps Carrick needs to shuffle the pack.

United win a free-kick about 25 yards from goal after Enzo Fernandez chases his own poor touch and fouls Tielemans.

Rashford to take... cracking hit, up and over the wall but the attempt bounces wide off the post.

United struggling to carve out clear openings, nobody was planning for the game to have this pattern with the home team dominating possession and City dropping off into a deep defensive shape. Nunes does exceptionally well to win a tackle, drive out from the back and find Cherki.

City threaten again after a poor defensive header by Dalot, with Semenyo fizzing in a low cross that is deflected behind for a corner with Fernandez lurking in the six-yard box. United have lost their way in the last 10 minutes, Dalot flagged offside unnecessarily.

There’s a reminder of City’s threat: Haaland spinning a pass wide right to Cherki who is in acres, but with Haaland in the middle and Semenyo on the edge of the box he crosses to nobody at the back stick.

He was not a starter in Carrick’s original game plan, but I wonder if United’s task now calls for Benjamin Sesko and some extra penalty-box presence and aerial threat. Guehi is having a very sound game at the back for City.

Both teams adjusting after the red card, Cherki and Semenyo are trying to put in a defensive shift in front of their full-backs. United enjoying the majority of possession, and Fernandes feeds Rashford with a delightful reverse pass but Rashford’s first touch was loose.

United will now be favourites to win this game, but Mainoo was required to block a goal-bound strike from Cherki after a corner was clear. City do have the ammunition to offer a threat on the break. They need the Haaland of his Dortmund days to attack big spaces on the counter.

Old Trafford is delirious because United’s scourge in so many derbies is off for an early shower. Fernandes and Foden were scrapping for the ball near the touchline, the United man had a nibble at Foden as he tried to protect the ball. But then Foden kicked up from the ground with his studs into the midriff of Fernandes. I don’t think he can have any complaints.

Although Foden’s sending off will certainly not have enhanced his prospects! Kicking out in retaliation at being kicked by Bruno Fernandes when he was on the ground.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL

The Old Trafford crowd are encouraged by what they are watching, but Enzo Fernandez takes some of the venom from their attacking momentum by winning a foul.

Then Ruben Dias clips a long ball forward over Dalot’s head which the right-back makes a mess of to Semenyo’s benefit, but the winger finds the gloves of Lammens with the cross. Just had to clear the goalkeeper and Haaland would have had an open goal.

England manager Thomas Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry are among those in attendance at Old Trafford ahead of Friday’s squad announcement, the first since the World Cup and ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign. There are plenty of players on show, on both sides ,who will hope to be in contention including Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford for United although Harry Maguire may have talked his way out of being considered after his reaction to not making the World Cup squad. For City there is Marc Guehi and Elliot Anderson - who both will be included - and it feels like a big game for Phil Foden.

Very wasteful from Haaland, after Bruno Fernandes’s stray wall pass back into midfield ran into his path. Neither picked a pass nor let fly with a shot and lost control of the ball.

At the other end, Guehi defends well against Rashford and City have a goal kick, but United have the upper hand in the game at the moment.

Cunha with a burst through City’s midfield and he is brought down by Fernandez. Just before that, City invited the pressure with a stray cross-field pass in their own defensive third which Guehi could not control. Mainoo then whips a teasing cross to the back post, but Rashford misread the flight of it and he was offside in any case.

City with a more sustained spell of possession in the United half, but Martinez defends well as Foden dribbles into the penalty area. Cunha then tries to release Rashford behind the City defence, but Dias covered well behind Guehi to intercept.

Promising counter-attack for United after Rashford pinches the ball off Foden in midfield, and the home team’s attacking quartet of players stream forward. Poor from Cunha though, dragging a shot well wide from an improbable distance.

Quite a composed start from City, Anderson enjoying plenty of touches in midfield. Fernandes tries to sweep a first-time pass out to Rashford wide left, but Nunes intercepts.

Then Fernandes’s next pass is more threatening, lofting a pass over the City defence for the run of Diogo Dalot but he cannot quite put the ball under his spell in the penalty area.

Rashford finds himself near the right touchline and finds room to drive inside with the ball, where he is sandwiched between Semenyo and Anderson. Free-kick for United in a crossing position right of centre, and from the second phase a Martinez cross flies into the gloves of Donnarumma.

An early glimpse of United’s slightly flimsy central midfield with Cherki finding space behind them and Enzo Fernandez’s strike from distance deflecting over the bar. Martinez heads Anderson’s delivery behind for another corner.

This time City take it short, but United clear their lines when the ball is crossed into the box.

The ball changes hands in midfield a couple of times in quick succession. Dalot pressing Semenyo but the winger gets away from him, but United win a challenge before Anderson nips in. Promising start if you want aggression and intensity.

Maguire is then penalised for a foul on Cherki in a more promising position for City, but from a free-kick taken short the flag goes up for offside. City claim there was a foul on Cherki from Fernandes.

United get the first Manchester derby of the season under way.

As expected, there is that banner above the mouth of the tunnel.

“THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE” banner is displayed above the Munich tunnel on the south west corner of the Stretford End.

Avram Glazer is in the directors’ box with Sir Jim Ratcliffe behind his co-owner.

We understand how important this game is and what it can do but it’s getting the balance, we know it’s a long season and we have to be consistent over a period of time. In some ways everything is on today, and it has to be, but it’s not everything in terms of the bigger picture.

Michael Carrick’s record has been outstanding, particularly at Old Trafford. They’ve been brilliant here and very difficult to beat.

If United drop points today, people will say it’s a bad start, if they win today, people will say they’re back.

If you had read Sam Wallace’s exclusive interview with United’s right-back you would know he was in line to make his 250th appearance for the club. Dalot did not want to take Carrick’s team selection for granted when talking about the milestone, but United’s manager is not replete with full-back options.

Struck by the nature of both midfields. If you look over the careers of Anderson-Fernandez-Cherki and Tielemans-Mainoo-Fernandes, Anderson is the only player of the six who has not played as a No 10 or advanced midfielder. The other five are not especially adept at covering ground and defensive actions, so this could well be wide open.

Thousands of Manchester United fans have been marching in protest at the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s running of the club.

Supporters have reacted with outrage to the club’s handling of a controversial anti ticket touting operation they felt unfairly singled out innocent fans.

And thousands have taken to the streets to voice their anger at how they feel they are being treated by the co-owners.

Plumes of red and green and yellow smoke filled the air as fans brandished banners and flags and chanted anti-Glazer and Ratcliffe songs.

“You take it all from fans and banning us for nothing. Premium prices all for greed,” read one banner.

One banner is a Stones Roses-themed number emblazoned with “Jim Aint The One”, a nod to Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the song This Is The One which is played at Old Trafford as the teams emerge from the tunnel.

Enzo Maresca has selected the more attacking option by playing Enzo Fernandez deeper alongside Elliot Anderson, rather than pushing the Argentine up a line and starting O’Reilly or Bouaddi. Still no Doku for City, and Foden has been preferred to Ndiaye out wide.

They are now 2-0 down against Brighton and Taiwo Awoniyi has been sent off for an elbow. Bar a miracle, it will be zero points from four games for Frank Lampard’s team.

Both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

Sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

To most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very important in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

It has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

With Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

#1429. New footage shows how goalkeeper in Spanish footballer's killer collision was fired-up in moments before 'reckless' tackle - as police probe medical team after opening homicide investigation

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER and NATALIA PENZA

Published: 05:13 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 08:28 EDT, 4 November 2026

New footage has revealed the tense moments before goalkeeper Jesus Owono launched a 'reckless' tackle that led to the death of Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Owono collided with opposing striker De Miguel in the latter stages of a hotly contested 2-2 draw in Spain's second division on Monday.

De Miguel immediately collapsed following the devastating blow in which Owono's knee appeared to strike the forward in the chest. He passed away in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

A homicide squad has launched an investigation as court officials explained any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation, with police now also probing the medical response to the incident.

Now, new footage taken from the stands has revealed how a fired-up Owono behaved in the moments leading up to the devastating collision.

The video shows how Owono had made his way to the other end of the pitch to get involved in a confrontation following a red card for opposing goalkeeper Dani Martin, before appearing to motion for him to make his way off the field of play.

Footage has revealed the heated build-up to the tackle that led to the death of Jesus de Miguel, which showed goalkeeper Jesus Owono arguing with his rival goalkeeper. (Source: X/Eldense_)

Fans have commented in Owono's involvement in an argument with opposing goalkeeper Dani Martin, who was sent off in the closing stages of the match (Source: X/Eldense_)

Martin and Owono appeared to continue their argument as they exchanged gestures as the Tenerife shot-stopper departed the scene.

The footage then captured Owono's wild celebrations - in which he leapt into the air and punched his fist - as Andorra FC scored an 88th minute equaliser.

'Here you have the images prior to the action by goalkeeper Owono, in the parts where he's not in focus — in one of them, he's confronting and saying things to the rival goalkeeper, and in the other, celebrating the goal right in the face of the Tenerife stands,' one fan wrote.

'He's a repeat offender when it comes to this kind of behavior.'

Another said: 'There isn't anyone from those of us who were in the stadium who didn't agree with the opinion that the entry was reckless. That it was an assault. It's clear that he didn't want the final outcome, but it's also clear that it wasn't an isolated incident.'

'I'm right behind that goal! Owono was completely unhinged! He came all the way to the rival goal to confront Dani, the Tenerife goalkeeper, over Lautaro's red card, and started gesticulating wildly at Dani to get him off the field after being sent off! This guy was totally out of his mind,' a third posted.

Former Real Madrid and Spain international goalkeeper Santiago Canizares, speaking on El Partidazo de COPE, conceded he believed Owono used ‘excessive force’ when going for the challenge.

Canizares, however, offered a defence of Owono by explaining the goalkeeper’s likely thought process and explained that they typically use their knees as protection and to help avoid collisions.

‘It's a goal-scoring opportunity, and what Owono has in his head is “I have to contest that ball,” ball or player,' Canizares said.

De Miguel died on Tuesday morning following a horrifying clash with Andorra FC goalkeeper Jesus Owono

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

‘For me, the problem is that Owono uses excessive force, and he lacks the physical dexterity to pull himself back when he sees he's won the duel.

‘He goes all out and goes all out until the end. That physical dexterity is key when only one of the two is contesting.

‘What happens in this case is that I think the momentum causes the knee to rise due to the force and excessive speed it brings.’

Andorra FC defender Lautaro Spatz has also defended his team-mate, writing that the goalkeeper has been 'deeply affected’ by the tragedy.

‘There are moments when football loses its meaning. Moments that mark you forever and make you realise how fragile life can be,’ Spatz wrote in a statement shared on social media.

‘What we went through is something none of us will ever forget. A tragedy that has left us completely broken, speechless, and with a sadness that is difficult to explain.

‘First and foremost, I want to express my deepest condolences and all my love to Jesús’s family, friends, and loved ones, as well as to the entire Tenerife community and the entire football family. Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated, and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy we never imagined we would experience on a football pitch,' he said.

‘I also want to say a few words to my teammate, goalkeeper, and friend, who is deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is. We know how much he is suffering right now and that he would never intend to hurt anyone.

‘In football, unforeseen events occur, but no one can imagine that one of them could end with such tragic consequences. Today, football doesn't matter. All that remains is to offer our condolences, show the utmost respect, and send all our strength to the family and to all those suffering this terrible loss. Rest in peace, Demi.'

Police investigating De Miguel's death are now probing the emergency medical response as well as the possibility rival goalie Jesus Owono's horror tackle could be involuntary manslaughter.

It emerged yesterday homicide squad officers based in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz had launched a probe as court officials explained any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation.

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Andorra FC goalkeeper Owono because the clash occurred during open play, although he is expected to be hit with a lengthy ban.

But overnight it emerged the police probe will also review the medical response to Monday's emergency and seek to address questions about whether Jesus de Miguel was given oxygen on the pitch and whether a defibrillator was used from the outset as well as issues around the assistance he received during his ambulance transfer.

The 30-year-old father-of-one died yesterday morning at Nuestra Senora Candelaria University Hospital after his second-division club revealed his neurological condition had worsened.

Medical personnel involved in the footballer's care are expected to be questioned and detectives will sift through medical reports as part of the probe.

Police investigating the death of CD Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel are probing the emergency medical response

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Andorra FC goalkeeper Owono

Well-placed sources told local press overnight there were 'certain discrepancies within the reports, or potential inaccuracies when compared to other evidence in the case' such as video footage recorded and posted on social media.

Respected island newspaper El Dia said: 'Among the issues currently under investigation, which according to sources remained unresolved as of yesterday, is whether the medical team who rushed from the sidelines to the centre of the pitch carrying a stretcher, a spinal board, and an Automated External Defibrillator to attend to the player, acted with due diligence during the more than six minutes they spent on the pitch before placing him on the spinal board for transport to an ambulance, which was stationed at one of the stadium access gates on La Mutine Street.'

It added: 'Investigators are also looking into an even more striking question.

'After a Guedel airway, a curved, semi-rigid oropharyngeal tube, was inserted into the player's mouth following his loss of consciousness, to prevent his tongue from obstructing his airway, was he also provided with oxygen during the resuscitation efforts on the pitch, as is required by protocol?

'According to sources, efforts are still underway to gather all available evidence to determine whether De Miguel was administered oxygen, either via a bag-valve mask (Ambu bag) or a face mask connected to one of the oxygen cylinders kept pitchside at the stadium.

'Sources indicate that this remains unresolved, at least regarding the medical care provided on the field of play.

'Furthermore, footage of the player being transported on a spinal board suggests that oxygen was not being administered during that process.

'Additionally, during the evacuation from the centre of the pitch to the ambulance, the player was carried on a spinal board by individuals who were moving at a jog.

Tributes have been paid to De Miguel outside the entrance to Tenerife's stadium

'The manner in which the patient was transported, which should never have been carried out in such a way, was highly dangerous to their physical well-being.'

Equatorial Guinea international Owono, who has lived in Spain since he was eight, was red-carded for kneeing Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel in the chest near the halfway line late into stoppage time. The match was suspended when the two sides were drawing 2-2.

Tragic Jesus, whose partner Maria and one-year-old daughter Carla were watching from the stands, was reportedly revived by paramedics on the pitch after going into cardiac arrest before being rushed to hospital.

His club confirmed around 9.30am local time yesterday morning he had died at a hospital in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz about 8am, saying they were 'heartbroken' and had a 'lump in their throats'.

It said in a statement, after revealing earlier the footballer's neurological condition had worsened: 'Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats, and unable to believe this is true, CD Tenerife announces the tragic passing of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, which occurred this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8am.

'There are no words of comfort, there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this profound sense of sorrow.

'We stand with his devastated family, his loved ones, and the entire 'tinerfeñismo' community, who today mourn this cruel outcome.

Owono is reportedly intending to apologise directly to de Miguel's family for his challenge and has made his social media private following abusive chants and messages he received (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono)

Owono is reportedly seeking to apologise to Jesus de Miguel's family before making any kind of public statement.

FC Andorra, reacting to news of the Tenerife striker's death in hospital, said yesterday morning: 'Heartbroken and devastated, we wish to extend our deepest condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, all his colleagues and friends, and to CD Tenerife.

Later today Jesus de Miguel's body is expected to be flown to the Spanish mainland so his funeral can take place in the town where his parents hail from.

The 30-year-old footballer's mum and dad travelled to Tenerife after being told about the severity of his injuries before confirmation this morning he had died in an island hospital.

They will now make the reverse trip to Madrid before travelling to Navahermosa in the province of Toledo 80 miles south-west of the Spanish capital which they have chosen as the place for the player's funeral.

Jesus's club revealed the location yesterday afternoon but said it was unable to say at this stage when exactly it would be.

Town hall officials in Navahermosa, which has a population of just over 3,500 inhabitants, said immediately after learning of the footballer's death: 'Since yesterday, we had held onto the hope that Jesus might overcome the toughest match of his life. However, we woke up today to the worst possible news.

'On behalf of the town hall, we wish to express our deepest sorrow at this tragic outcome. We want to extend all our love, support, and affection to his family, friends, and everyone who is feeling this loss today.

'There are no words that can ease such profound pain, but please know that we are by your side and that we share in your sadness.

'Jesus, you have always been, and will always remain, a source of pride for us.

'Today, with broken hearts, we must say goodbye, but we will hold onto your memory. Rest in peace.'

Emiliano Garcia-Page, president of Spain's Castilla-La Mancha region which includes Navahermosa and the province of Toledo where a train crash last Wednesday claimed the lives of 69 people, added in his own statement: 'I am at a loss for words; the passing of footballer Jesus de Miguel, while doing what he loved most and what he had fought so hard for, playing football, is heartbreaking news.

'My thoughts are with his family, who hail from the municipality of Navahermosa in the province of Toledo. My deepest condolences.'

The entire CD Tenerife squad will travel to Navahermosa to pay their last respects to their teammate.

Flags outside the town hall flew at half mast today.

The National Police in the island capital Santa Cruz has yet to release an official statement about its ongoing probe.

A minute's silence was held before Champions League matches in memory of De Miguel on Tuesday

But a force spokesman said yesterday evening: 'An investigation is underway into the circumstances surrounding the incident which led to Jesus de Miguel's death which is being conducted by the homicide unit.

'It has been opened because the death was not the result of natural causes and it will seek to determine whether in terms of the law, an involuntary manslaughter could have been committed.'

The report police draft as a result of their probe will be submitted to a local judge whose job it will be to decide whether to take the matter further.

A Canary Islands court source described the collision between the two footballers as 'an accidental collision on the playing field.'

But he added: 'Any death not resulting from natural causes, referred to as a 'forensic death,' whether due to an accident or other factors, automatically triggers a judicial investigation, which is the case here.'

Court officials said this morning they weren't able to comment on when they expected to receive the police report into the drama.

One said: 'At the moment the investigation is still in the hands of police who will submit their report to a court in Santa Cruz once officers have completed their work.'

#1428. Everton Women Unwrap New Partnership With Nestlé Confectionery

Everton Women has announced a new multi-year partnership with Nestlé Confectionery, bringing one of the world's most recognisable food and beverage companies into the Club's growing portfolio of commercial partners.

The agreement will see Nestlé Confectionery become the 'Official Chocolate and Grab Bag Sweet Partner of Everton Women' and an 'Official Supplier of Hill Dickinson Stadium', with household favourites including KitKat, Smarties, Rowntree's, Aero, Lion, Yorkie, Milkybar and Quality Street set to feature across both venues.

At Goodison Park, Nestlé Confectionery will have a prominent presence through pitchside LED advertising, big-screen exposure and matchday activations designed to engage supporters, alongside opportunities to showcase its products at food kiosks and points of sale.

Supporters and visitors to Hill Dickinson Stadium will also be able to enjoy Nestlé Confectionery's popular range of products, extending the brand's presence across both of Everton's iconic stadiums.

The agreement represents Everton Women's second dedicated commercial partnership, following last year's deal with GGM Gastro, with further Everton Women's-focused partnerships set to be announced.

The growing interest from major businesses reflects the opportunities being created around Everton Women, with the team's move to Goodison Park offering prospective partners a unique combination of footballing heritage, an iconic stadium and access to new audiences as the women's game continues to develop.

Andrew Middleton, President of Business Operations at Everton, said:  “We are delighted to welcome Nestlé Confectionery as a partner of Everton Women and an Official Supplier of Hill Dickinson Stadium.

“Like Everton, Nestlé’s brands have been part of family life for generations, making this a natural fit for our supporters and matchday experience. Together, we will create engaging moments across both venues and bring these iconic products closer to our audiences.

“This partnership is another important step in Everton Women’s continued growth, and we look forward to working with Nestlé to bring it to life.”

Gail Stove, OOH Confectionery Lead for Nestlé UK & Ireland, said: "Nestlé Confectionery is excited to be an Official Partner of Everton Women and Official Supplier of Hill Dickinson Stadium.

"We can’t wait to share our beloved brands with visitors at these brilliant venues.

“Working collaboratively with Everton Football Club, we’ll bring the No.1 confectionery single within the leisure channel, KitKat® 4 Finger, along with other iconic Nestlé Confectionery brands for everyone to enjoy.”

Further details of Nestlé Confectionery's planned matchday activations and opportunities for Everton supporters to engage with its brands will be announced in the coming months.

#1427. Venousization enables angiogenesis in the absence of VEGFR signalling

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

The vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) ligand and its main receptor VEGFR2 are considered to be essential for endothelial differentiation, proliferation, sprouting and survival1. Blood vessels cannot form in growing embryos or tissues when VEGF–VEGFR2 signalling is compromised in all cells2,3. The anti-VEGF antibody, which can block angiogenesis in cancer, wound healing or ischaemic diseases, is among the most widely used antibodies in the clinic. However, vascular resistance to anti-VEGF therapy has been reported4,5. Here we used iFlpMosaics and iSuRe–HadCre to induce and track genetic mosaics of endothelial cells (ECs) lacking VEGFR2 during the entire embryonic and postnatal development. These Vegfr2-knockout (Vegfr2KO) ECs adapted, proliferated normally and competed with wild-type cells over time, eventually forming a substantial portion of the vascular network in most organs. Vegfr2KO ECs could not sprout during the first wave of angiogenesis in most tissues, because this process is highly VEGF-dependent and favours growth and mobilization of wild-type ECs. However, owing to their inability to respond to VEGF, Vegfr2KO ECs became dominant in veins, which represented a long-term and continuous source of ECs for subsequent waves of VEGF-independent angiogenesis. Comparative single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of ECs with acute and long-term loss of VEGFR2 identified both common and organ-specific molecular mechanisms of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss. These included significant endothelial venousization and upregulation of ligands for VEGFR1 and VEGFR3. VEGFR1 only partially compensated for VEGFR2 loss in capillary ECs, whereas VEGFR3 compensated only in arterial ECs. Loss of the three VEGF receptors did not compromise venous growth. Notably, loss of the master regulator of venous development, NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), significantly compromised expansion of Vegfr2KO ECs. This work has implications for our understanding of the role of VEGF receptors in angiogenesis and demonstrates venousization as a mechanism of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss during angiogenesis.

VEGF is frequently targeted in clinical settings to suppress tumour angiogenesis, metastasis and retina disease6. However, resistance to VEGF-blocking antibodies arises over time, which limits the effectiveness of such treatments4,5,7,8. By contrast, resistance to loss of VEGF signalling has not been reported during physiological vascular development.

Embryos or postnatal tissues lacking activity of the VEGF signalling pathway in all cells fail to develop vessels3. VEGFR2 (encoded by the Kdr (also known as Vegfr2) gene in mice) is the most important VEGF receptor and has been shown to be essential for angiogenesis in all vascular development contexts studied so far1,9. Germline mutants for this gene completely lack blood vessels and die very early during embryonic development2, and mouse embryos chimeras formed by wild-type and Vegfr2-knockout (Vegfr2KO) progenitor cells cannot form endothelial cells (ECs)10. Conditional deletion of Vegfr2 with Tie2–Cre after endothelial differentiation11, or in postnatal tissues with Cdh5–CreERT2, also strongly impairs angiogenesis12, without any evidence of genetic compensation or resistance.

Despite a large body of literature showing that VEGFR2 is essential for endothelial differentiation, proliferation, migration and survival, previous studies involving deletion of Vegfr2 in all ECs (Vegfr2iDEC) during embryonic or postnatal organ development could only analyse its effect on angiogenesis for a relatively short period of time. Its essential role in vascular development and hence in tissue development and organ function causes severe impairment of angiogenesis and premature lethality of Vegfr2iDEC embryos and postnatal animals; thus, such studies have been unable to determine whether ECs can adapt to loss of VEGFR2 over time or make certain organ vascular beds in the complete absence of VEGF–VEGFR2 signalling.

Here we used iFlpMosaics13 and iSuRe–HadCre14 to mosaically induce and longitudinally track Vegfr2KO ECs, enabling us to assess the role of this gene during the entire embryonic and postnatal vascular development of different organs. We found that despite its essential role during the initial wave of embryonic and postnatal angiogenesis, VEGF–VEGFR2 signalling is dispensable for many subsequent angiogenic processes originating from veins. Vegfr2KO ECs expand and out-compete wild-type ECs in venous vessels, which serve as a continuous source of these mutant cells for angiogenesis in most organs. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) showed that Vegfr2KO ECs adapt over time through upregulation of ligands for other VEGF receptors and through increased expression of venous-specific genes, particularly Nr2f2. Targeting these adaptive and resistance-associated molecular mechanisms prevents expansion of ECs following prolonged loss of VEGFR2 signalling.

Given the essential role of VEGFR2 in early angiogenesis and embryonic development, we induced mosaic loss of VEGFR2 with iFlpMosaics13 to investigate whether mutant cells could adapt and form new vessels over time. This technology enables FlpO-dependent ratiometric induction and tracking over long periods of time of cells expressing MTomato-2A-Cre (knockout for any floxed gene) or MYFP (wild type). To induce these mosaics, we used the Apln-FlpO allele, which is expressed in the first angiogenic and sprouting ECs at embryonic day 8.5 (E8.5) and throughout vascular development. In female embryos, the X-chromosome-located Apln–FlpO allele is mosaically silenced15 and expressed only in a fraction (23–50%) of ECs, generating relatively few mutant and wild-type cells, which we found to be compatible with embryonic development (Fig. 1a and Extended Data Fig. 1a). Analysis of major organs of Apln-FlpO iFlpMosaic mice showed that ECs with full loss of VEGFR2 (Vegfr2KO-E8.5–P7) were able to survive and proliferate during embryonic development and until postnatal day 7 (P7), with only a relatively minor competitive disadvantage (2–7-fold) compared with wild-type cells (Fig. 1b). This competitive disadvantage was more pronounced in the lung and kidney endothelium and less so in brain ECs (Fig. 1b,c and Extended Data Fig. 1a–c). As Apln-FlpO is constitutively active and can drive recombination at later stages of embryonic development, we also induced Vegfr2 deletion using 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OHT) at E10.5 and E12.5 in embryos carrying Cdh5-CreERT2, iSuRe-HadCre and an iMb2-Mosaic16 control reporter that recombines independently of Vegfr2 deletion (Extended Data Fig. 2a–c). This resulted in a maximum of 1–6% recombined ECs, as opposed to 23–50% with Apln-FlpO. However, this recapitulated the trend in which brain ECs were least affected by VEGFR2 loss, followed by those in the heart, liver, lung and kidney (Extended Data Fig. 2b,c).

a, Schematic of iFlpMosaics induced by Apln-FlpO from E8.5 to P7. b, log2 ratio of MTomato+/MYFP+ within CD31+CD45− cells detected by FACS for the indicated organs. The absolute fold change of the ratio of Vegfr2KO ECs versus the ratio of control Tomato+ cells is indicated in red. c, Representative gating scheme for the ratiometric analysis (see also Extended Data Fig. 1a). d, Representative confocal micrographs of control and Vegfr2KO-E8.5–P7 retinas immunostained for Tomato, YFP and ERG (which labels EC nuclei). Heatmap, XY dot plot and charts showing the zonal distribution and percentage of Tomato+Cre+ cells when equal numbers of randomly selected YFP+ and Tomato+ cells were plotted (see method in Extended Data Fig. 3a). Right, log2 ratio of Tomato+/YFP+ cells detected in whole-mount retina immunostainings, showing an overall competitive disadvantage of Vegfr2KO cells in the mapped retinas. e, Representative confocal micrographs of retinas immunostained for ERG at P7, from pups injected with 4-OHT at P1. Heatmap, XY dot plot and charts showing distribution of MTomato+ERG+ (wild-type, Vegfr2HET or Vegfr2KO) cells in space in relation to MTomato−ERG+ (wild-type) cells. f, Bar plot contrasting the relative frequency of the indicated cells in the indicated areas and genotypes. g, log2 fold change of Vegfr2KO-E8.5–P7 and Vegfr2IECKO-P1–P7 cells relative to the respective control wild-type cells. Numbers indicate fold change (×) between the two groups. Data are presented as the mean ± s.d. Scale bars, 100 μm. A, arteries; AF, angiogenic front; dist., distance; freq., frequency; IntCap, intermediate capillaries; LE, leading edge; MA, mature area; V, veins; WT, wild type.

VEGFR2 activity is essential for NOTCH activation and the development of arteries17,18,19. Arteries are formed by tip ECs20, which have the highest level of VEGF–VEGFR2 signalling and guide vascular growth. Our high-resolution spatial zonation data with long-term iFlpMosaics showed that Vegfr2KO-E8.5–P7 ECs were significantly enriched in veins and surrounding capillaries, and avoided angiogenic front capillaries or tip ECs, but were able to form arteries (Fig. 1d; see also Extended Data Fig. 3a for the heatmapping method).

To complement these results, we intercrossed the Vegfr2 floxed allele with Cdh5-CreERT2 and iSuRe-HadCre14 alleles to ensure fast (24 h; Extended Data Fig. 3b,c) and effective mosaic genetic deletion and full loss of VEGFR2 protein and downstream targets in ECs (Cdh5 expressing), after a single injection of 4-OHT. Vegfr2IECKO-P1–P7 ECs were located mainly in veins and surrounding capillaries, as well as in the more proximal and mature segments of retina arteries (Fig. 1e). This indicates that when Vegfr2KO ECs are induced in the initial retina sprouting plexus at P1, they can make arteries forming from P1 to P3. However, owing to their inability to continue to sprout and form tip cells at the leading edge, they cannot participate in the subsequent arterial development process occurring from P3 to P7, which in the retina is dependent on incorporation of new tip cells21.

Notably, compared with Vegfr2IECKO-P1−P7 ECs, Vegfr2KO-E8.5−P7 ECs were more frequent at the leading edge and angiogenic front capillaries (Fig. 1f,g) and were still able to make arteries. This suggests that embryonic Vegfr2KO-E8.5−P7 ECs can adapt to long-term loss of VEGFR2 and contribute to venous vascular growth, tip cells and arteries at postnatal stages.

We next investigated how Vegfr2KO ECs could compete with wild-type cells and contribute to growing vascular networks over long periods of time, given the proposed important role of this pathway in EC proliferation1,22. During angiogenesis, there are two main locations for EC proliferation: the capillary angiogenic front and veins (Fig. 2a). We found that the surviving Vegfr2KO-E8.5−P7 ECs proliferated (as determined by Ki-67 detection) as well as wild-type cells in postnatal brain, heart and lung vessels (Fig. 2b).

a, Representative confocal micrograph of a control P7 retina immunostained for the proliferation marker Ki-67 and the EC nuclear marker ERG. The chart shows the frequency of Ki-67+ERG+ (pink pseudocolored) nuclei in different vascular zones. b, Representative confocal micrographs of the indicated organs of Vegfr2KO-E8.5–P7 mice at P7, immunostained for YFP, Tomato, ERG and Ki-67. Yellow arrows indicate YFP+Ki-67+ cells and magenta arrows Tomato+Ki-67+ ECs. c, Representative confocal micrographs of control and Vegfr2IECKO-P1–P20 retinas induced at P1 and analysed at P20. Heatmap, XY dot plot and chart showing that Vegfr2IECKO-P1–P20 ECs grow in veins and surrounding capillaries. d,e, Representative confocal micrographs of retinas immunostained for cleaved caspase 3 and respective quantification charts, showing increased apoptosis of Vegfr2IECKO-P4–P7 but not Vegfr2IECKO-P1–P7 ECs. f, Representative confocal micrographs of the indicated organs of control and Vegfr2IECKO-P4–P7 mice induced at P4 and analysed at P7. Arrows indicate recombined ECs (Tomato+) that are Ki-67+ (yellow) and Ki-67− (white), respectively. Chart shows the percentage of Tomato+ ECs positive for Ki-67. Data are presented as mean ± s.d. Scale bars, 100 μm (a,c–e), 50 μm (b,f). Cap., capillaries; CC3, cleaved caspase 3; Ctrl, control; DCap, distal capillaries; IntCap, intermediate capillaries; PCap, proximal capillaries. *Adjusted P < 0.05.

Venous ECs provide a continuous source of ECs for angiogenesis and these migrate against the blood flow to capillaries and then towards arterial vessels20,23,24. When we induced Vegfr2KO ECs for longer periods of time, from P1 to P20 (Vegfr2IECKO-P1–P20), we observed that mutant cells stayed in the vein stem, where they proliferated and gradually outcompeted wild-type cells, which moved outwards towards the VEGF-rich leading edge and adjacent capillaries (Fig. 2c). This preferential occupation of the venous stem niche by Vegfr2KO ECs allowed them to continue proliferating for longer periods of time and later to form most of the perivenous capillary vessels and the deeper vascular plexus that developed during a second wave of VEGF-independent angiogenesis from P7 to P20 (Extended Data Fig. 4a,b). This was consistent with previous findings showing that the tip cells that dive to form the deeper vascular plexus in the retina lack expression of the VEGFR2 signalling target gene Esm1; instead, their migration is dependent on other pathways such as Alk or TGFβ and WNT signalling25,26,27.

Together, these data show that VEGFR2 function is essential for the initial sprouting angiogenesis driven by high VEGF levels in hypoxic embryos and organs but not for the development of veins and perivenous capillaries or the subsequent steps of capillary angiogenesis and remodelling that occur after the first vascular plexus is formed in various organs. Thus, by forming veins, which are known to provide a continuous source of ECs for angiogenesis23, Vegfr2KO ECs can continue to proliferate and participate in subsequent steps of vascular development for long periods of time.

We previously observed that the distribution of Vegfr2KO ECs in the retina plexus at P7 differed between animals with long-term (Vegfr2KO-E8.5–P7) and short-term (Vegfr2IECKO-P1–P7) mosaic deletion of Vegfr2. Vegfr2KO-E8.5–P7 ECs were more frequent at the leading edge and angiogenic front than Vegfr2IECKO-P1–P7 ECs (Fig. 1f,g). Vegfr2KO-E8.5–P7 ECs also proliferated normally (Fig. 2b). Therefore, we hypothesized that Vegfr2KO-E8.5–P7 ECs might be genetically rewired and adapt over time to loss of the most important receptor for VEGF.

To assess the early response of ECs to loss of VEGFR2, we first analysed apoptosis markers in growing retina vessels, as VEGFR2 has been shown to regulate EC survival. Vegfr2IECKO-P4–P7 mice showed a very significant increase in the number of apoptotic (cleaved caspase 3 positive) ECs (Fig. 2d). This apoptosis was a reaction to the acute loss of VEGFR2, as Vegfr2KO-E8.5–P7 or even Vegfr2IECKO-P1–P7 mice did not show any apoptotic ECs (Fig. 2e), suggesting adaptation of the surviving cells over time. When the acute loss of Vegfr2 was induced in all ECs, we observed an immediate depletion of Vegfr2KO ECs from the VEGF-high angiogenic front, but not from veins or more mature vessels (Extended Data Fig. 4c). Therefore, even though many ECs in the retina plexus showed upregulation of the apoptosis marker in the first days after Vegfr2 loss (Fig. 2d), only the angiogenic ECs that were exposed to high VEGF levels at the time of Vegfr2 deletion died (Extended Data Fig. 4c).

We also found that Vegfr2IECKO-P4–P7 ECs were significantly less proliferative than control cells only in the heart and kidney (Fig. 2f), whereas the proliferation of Vegfr2KO-E8.5–P7 ECs was similar to that of controls (Fig. 2b). This suggests that Vegfr2KO ECs adapt over time and are later able to proliferate in these organs. In the newborn retina, deletion of Vegfr2 did not affect the proliferation of surviving ECs in any segment (Extended Data Fig. 4d), indicating that in this organ VEGFR2 mainly controls EC migration and survival, not proliferation.

Together, our data suggest that ECs lacking VEGF signalling during active angiogenesis suffer an acute VEGFR2 withdrawal effect, followed by a period of adaptation to the loss, after which they can form new vessels. ECs that are more distant from the VEGF source, and therefore have less VEGF signalling, adapt better to the loss and can expand over time, particularly in veins and perivenous vessels.

To further confirm the insensitivity of more mature ECs to loss of VEGFR2 signalling, we deleted Vegfr2 in several adult quiescent vascular beds for 2 weeks. Only the quiescent sinusoidal liver endothelium showed a strong sensitivity and loss of Vegfr2KO ECs, whereas only the kidney endothelium showed significantly lower proliferation (Extended Data Fig. 5), suggesting that only fenestrated or discontinuous mature endothelial vessels present in these organs remain sensitive to VEGFR2 loss.

Given the observed differences in the biology of Vegfr2IECKO-P4–P7 and Vegfr2KO-E8.5–P7 ECs, we performed scRNA-seq of these cells and respective control Tomato+ cells to identify possible differences in their transcriptional profiles and potential mechanisms of adaptation to loss of VEGFR2 signalling in distinct organ vascular beds.

Although VEGFR2 is a central regulator of angiogenesis and widely regarded as essential for EC biology, Vegfr2IECKO-P4–P7 ECs showed only modest changes in their transcriptome (Fig. 3 and Extended Data Fig. 6), even though VEGFR2 protein and downstream signalling were lost already within the first 24 h following 4-OHT administration (Extended Data Fig. 3b,c). In general, the expression of genes related to sprouting or tip cell biology was decreased, whereas that of genes related to apoptosis and vascular permeability was increased in all organs analysed (Fig. 3a,b). However, considerable differences were observed among organs.

In the brain, clusters of proliferating (S–G2–M) ECs expressing venous capillaries markers were increased after Vegfr2 deletion for 3 days (Fig. 3c–f). This was consistent with higher clonal expansion of Vegfr2KO ECs from P1 to P20 in this organ (Extended Data Fig. 7a). Clusters comprising capillary and activated or angiogenic ECs (with high expression of Apln, Adm, Mcam, Lamb1 and Angpt2) were decreased (Fig. 3d–f). In total, only 569 genes were significantly deregulated (Fig. 3g). Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed an increase in the expression of E2F and MYC target genes, as well as G2M, DNA repair and mitotic spindle genes, confirming the increase in EC proliferation (Fig. 3h and Extended Data Fig. 7a). The expression of most tip cell marker genes was decreased in Vegfr2IECKO-P4–P7 brain ECs (Fig. 3i and Extended Data Fig. 6a–f).

In contrast to those in the brain, Vegfr2IECKO-P4–P7 capillary ECs in the heart were significantly less proliferative (Fig. 3j–m and Extended Data Fig. 7b), matching the 54% decrease in Ki-67 percentage observed in sections (Fig. 2f). The proportion of mutant ECs found in bigger vessels (arteries and veins) was increased 2- to 4-fold (Fig. 3k–m), suggesting a proportional fast depletion of Vegfr2KO capillary ECs in only 3 days. Unlike in the brain, GSEA of Vegfr2KO heart ECs showed the expected decrease in expression of E2F and MYC target genes, as well as decreases in expression of G2M, mitotic spindle and tip cell genes (Fig. 3n–p), in accordance with the decrease in proliferation and sprouting of Vegfr2IECKO-P4–P7 heart ECs. Vegfr2KO heart ECs also showed upregulation of genes related to apoptosis and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (Fig. 3n–p), as has been shown previously for ECs losing ERK signalling28.

In contrast to the results for brain and heart, we found no significant difference in the proportions of proliferating cells among control and Vegfr2IECKO-P4–P7 ECs in lung (Extended Data Fig. 6g–j), as shown by immunostaining for Ki-67 and clonal analysis (Fig. 2f and Extended Data Fig. 7c). The proportion of the vein cluster was only slightly increased, and the capillary cluster was slightly decreased. Despite the lack of significant changes in cluster proportions, GSEA showed increased TNF signalling through NF-κB, hypoxia and reactive oxygen species signalling and a decrease in the interferon response (Extended Data Fig. 6k,l). In lung, there was only a small trend of decreased expression of tip cell marker genes (Extended Data Fig. 6m), and several genes related to apoptosis were upregulated (Extended Data Fig. 6l,m).

In the kidney, similar to the heart, Vegfr2 deletion for 3 days led to an increase in the relative proportion of ECs of bigger vessels (arteries and veins), suggesting fast depletion of a fraction of capillary ECs in only 3 days (Extended Data Fig. 6n–q). Proliferation and clonal expansion of kidney capillary ECs were also reduced (Extended Data Figs. 6o,q and 7d), as shown by immunostaining for Ki-67 (Fig. 2f). GSEA showed the expected decrease in expression of E2F, G2M and mitotic spindle genes and an increase in the expression of genes related to p53, xenobiotic metabolism and apoptosis (Extended Data Fig. 6r,s), indicative of cellular stress in kidney ECs after short-term Vegfr2 deletion from P4 to P7. Similar to brain and heart ECs, the expression of tip cell marker genes was also decreased in kidney Vegfr2IECKO-P4–P7 ECs (Extended Data Fig. 6t).

Following our analysis of Vegfr2IECKO-P4–P7 ECs, we performed scRNA-seq of Vegfr2KO-E8.5–P7 ECs of distinct organs to identify potential differences in gene expression related to long-term adaptation of cells to loss of VEGFR2 (Extended Data Fig. 8a). In contrast to Vegfr2IECKO-P4–P7 ECs, Vegfr2KO-E8.5–P7 ECs exhibited predominantly upregulation rather than downregulation of genes, including marked upregulation of several venous-enriched genes (compare Figs. 3a,b and 4a).
